rmt-2013-gen-01.title: Fraction of pigeons
rmt-2013-gen-01.body:
Pigeons are $1-\frac23-\frac18=\frac{5}{24}$ of the birds. So the total is $5\div\frac5{24}=24$ birds, and robins are $\frac23\cdot24=16$.

**Answer: 16**

rmt-2013-gen-02.title: Find the limiting ingredient
rmt-2013-gen-02.body:
Dough allows $200$ pizzas, cheese $20\div\frac14=80$, sauce $20\div\frac16=120$, and toppings in total $(15+5+5+10)\div\frac13=105$. The smallest is cheese: $80$ pizzas.

**Answer: 80**

rmt-2013-gen-03.title: Choose from the 8 cards
rmt-2013-gen-03.body:
A deck has $4$ queens and $4$ jacks, $8$ cards in all. The liked hands are all $5$-card subsets of these: $\binom85=56$.

**Answer: 56**

rmt-2013-gen-04.title: Multiples of 210
rmt-2013-gen-04.body:
The first four primes are $2,3,5,7$ with product $210$. $210\cdot42=8820<9000$ and $210\cdot43=9030>9000$. So the answer is $9030$.

**Answer: 9030**

rmt-2013-gen-05.title: Diagonals
rmt-2013-gen-05.body:
Let the diagonals be $d$ and $2d$. The area is $\frac{d\cdot2d}2=d^2=36$, so $d=6$ and the diagonals are $6$ and $12$. They are perpendicular bisectors of each other, so a side is $\sqrt{3^2+6^2}=3\sqrt5$ and the perimeter is $12\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $12\sqrt5$**

rmt-2013-gen-07.title: Compare the two lengths
rmt-2013-gen-07.body:
The fly goes along the space diagonal: $\sqrt{1+1+1}=\sqrt3$. The ant's shortest path crosses two adjacent faces; unfolded they form a $2\times1$ rectangle whose diagonal is $\sqrt{2^2+1^2}=\sqrt5$. The fly's path is shorter by $\sqrt5-\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $\sqrt5-\sqrt3$**

rmt-2013-gen-08.title: Count mismatched outfits
rmt-2013-gen-08.body:
With $n$ pairs, a mismatched outfit is a left shoe and a right shoe from different pairs: $n(n-1)$ choices. In year $2013+k$ there are $n=2^k$ pairs. For $2017$ ($n=16$): $16\cdot15=240<500$. For $2018$ ($n=32$): $32\cdot31=992\ge500$. So the earliest year is $2018$.

**Answer: 2018**

rmt-2013-gen-11.title: Lateral cone plus hemisphere
rmt-2013-gen-11.body:
The cone has radius $1$ and height $2\sqrt2$, so its slant height is $\sqrt{1+8}=3$ and its lateral area is $\pi\cdot1\cdot3=3\pi$. The open top of the cone is covered by the hemisphere of radius $1$, whose curved surface is $2\pi$. Total: $5\pi$.

**Answer: $5\pi$ square inches**

rmt-2013-gen-12.title: Discriminant
rmt-2013-gen-12.body:
Real solutions exist iff $25-4c\ge0$, i.e. $c\le\frac{25}4$. The greatest value is $\frac{25}4$.

**Answer: $\frac{25}4$**

rmt-2013-gen-13.title: Lower bound and a strategy
rmt-2013-gen-13.body:
With only $3$ red points, Blue's points can block: after Red's first two points, Blue puts a point between them, and whatever Red does with the third point, the line through three red points either contains that blue point between two of them or is not a line through all three. So Red needs at least $4$ moves.

Strategy for $4$: Red places $r_1$, Blue $b_1$. Red places $r_2$ not collinear with $r_1,b_1$. Blue must put $b_2$ between $r_1$ and $r_2$ (else Red wins by a third point on line $r_1r_2$). Red places $r_3$ between $b_1$ and $b_2$ (so Blue cannot threaten to win by forming his own line). Now $r_3$ together with $r_1$ and with $r_2$ gives two separate lines with no blue point between the red points, each needing a third red point. Blue can only spoil one of them, and Red completes the other on move $4$.

**Answer: 4**

rmt-2013-gen-14.title: Compare times
rmt-2013-gen-14.body:
The distance from $(0,5)$ to $(17,39)$ is $\sqrt{17^2+34^2}=17\sqrt5$. Rob needs $\frac{17\sqrt5}2$ seconds, Peter needs $\frac{17\sqrt5}3$ seconds. Peter starts later by $t=\frac{17\sqrt5}2-\frac{17\sqrt5}3=\frac{17\sqrt5}6$.

**Answer: $\frac{17\sqrt5}6$**

rmt-2013-gen-15.title: Count small triangles
rmt-2013-gen-15.body:
Split the hexagon into $6$ equilateral triangles from the centre, and each of these into $4$ small equilateral triangles by joining midpoints: $24$ small triangles. Triangle $PQR$ is made of $9$ of them. The probability is $\frac9{24}=\frac38$.

**Answer: $\frac38$**

rmt-2013-gen-16.title: Glue the pairs
rmt-2013-gen-16.body:
Treat Alice-Bob as one block and Claire-Derek as another: $6$ objects, $6!=720$ orders. Each pair can be ordered in $2$ ways: $720\cdot2\cdot2=2880$.

**Answer: 2880**

rmt-2013-gen-17.title: Use the diameter
rmt-2013-gen-17.body:
The hypotenuse of an inscribed right triangle is a diameter, so it splits the disc into two semicircles of area $\frac{25\pi}2$. The legs cut one semicircle into the triangle (legs $5\sqrt2$, area $\frac{(5\sqrt2)^2}2=25$) and two segments whose total area is $\frac{25\pi}2-25\approx14.3$. The triangle (area $25$) and the other semicircle ($\approx39.3$) are larger than that, and each of the two segments is smaller than the triangle, so the two smallest regions are exactly these two segments. Their total is $\frac{25\pi}2-25$.

**Answer: $\frac{25\pi}2-25$**

rmt-2013-gen-18.title: Marginal costs
rmt-2013-gen-18.body:
The extra space for each additional tree is $1,3,5,7,\dots$ for apples, always $5$ for apricots, and $1,7,19,\dots$ for plums. These are non-decreasing for each type, so the cheapest way to plant $10$ trees is to take the $10$ smallest extra costs overall: $1$ (apple), $1$ (plum), $3$ (apple), and seven $5$s (from the third apple tree and apricots). The total is $1+1+3+7\cdot5=40$. For example, $3$ apple, $6$ apricot, $1$ plum trees take $9+30+1=40$.

**Answer: 40**

rmt-2013-gen-18.title: Check by enumeration
rmt-2013-gen-18.body:
Trying every split $(a,r,p)$ with $a+r+p=10$ and cost $a^2+5r+p^3$ by computer gives minimum $40$ (for instance at $(3,6,1)$ and $(2,7,1)$).

**Answer: 40**

rmt-2013-gen-19.title: Right angle
rmt-2013-gen-19.body:
The area is $\frac12\cdot2\cdot3\sin\theta=3\sin\theta\le3$, so equality forces $\theta=90^\circ$. The third side is $\sqrt{2^2+3^2}=\sqrt{13}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{13}$**

rmt-2013-gen-20.title: Concentric rings
rmt-2013-gen-20.body:
The score is $5$ for $x\le1$, $4$ for $1<x\le2$, and so on down to $1$ for $4<x\le5$. The rings have areas $\pi,3\pi,5\pi,7\pi,9\pi$ out of $25\pi$. Expected score $=\frac{5\cdot1+4\cdot3+3\cdot5+2\cdot7+1\cdot9}{25}=\frac{55}{25}=\frac{11}5$.

**Answer: $\frac{11}5$**

rmt-2013-gen-22.title: Structure of minimal sets
rmt-2013-gen-22.body:
Let $S$ be minimally competent of size $k$; it contains $k$. If $S$ had an element $j<k$, then a subset of $S$ of size $j$ containing $j$ would be a proper competent subset, a contradiction. So $S=\{k\}\cup T$ with $T\subseteq\{k+1,\dots,10\}$ and $|T|=k-1$. Conversely every such set works: a proper subset of size $m<k$ has all elements $\ge k>m$, so it does not contain $m$. We need $k-1\le10-k$, i.e. $k\le5$. The count is $\sum_{k=1}^5\binom{10-k}{k-1}=1+8+21+20+5=55$.

**Answer: 55**

rmt-2013-gen-22.title: Brute force
rmt-2013-gen-22.body:
Enumerating all $1023$ nonempty subsets of $A$ and testing that the set is competent while no proper subset is gives exactly $55$.

**Answer: 55**

rmt-2013-gen-24.title: Coordinates
rmt-2013-gen-24.body:
Put the right angle at the origin with legs $1$ (along $x$) and $\sqrt3$ (along $y$). The circumcenter is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, $\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)$. The inradius is $r=\frac{1+\sqrt3-2}2=\frac{\sqrt3-1}2$, so the incenter is $(r,r)$. Then the squared distance is $\left(r-\frac12\right)^2+\left(r-\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)^2=\left(\frac{\sqrt3-2}2\right)^2+\left(\frac{-1}2\right)^2=\frac{7-4\sqrt3}4+\frac14=2-\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $2-\sqrt3$**

rmt-2013-gen-25.title: Count the fillings
rmt-2013-gen-25.body:
The first three columns hold any arrangement of $1,\dots,9$: $9!$ ways; call the rows' number sets $S_1,S_2,S_3$. For the last three columns, first choose which numbers go in each row: row $i$ may not use numbers of $S_i$. If $n_{ij}$ numbers of $S_j$ go to row $i$ ($i\ne j$), the conditions force $n_{12}=n_{23}=n_{31}=t$ and the others $3-t$ for $t=0,1,2,3$. For $t=0,3$ there is $1$ way each; for $t=1,2$ there are $3^3=27$ ways each. So $2+54=56$ ways to split. Then each row's three numbers can be ordered in $3!$ ways: $6^3$. So $N=9!\cdot56\cdot6^3$.

$v_2(9!)=4+2+1=7$, $v_2(56)=3$, $v_2(6^3)=3$, so $k=7+3+3=13$.

**Answer: 13**
